column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|03-27|1969|Μαράια Κάρεϊ|Mariah Carey|Mariah Carey is an American singer with a voice of five octaves. She has released many hits, such as "Hero", "We Belong Together" and "All I Want for Christmas Is You", and has had many songs at number one on American charts.

bio|03-27|1972|Μαουρίτς Κορνέλις Έσερ|M. C. Escher|M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist. He became known for his works with optical illusions, impossible shapes and mathematical symmetries, such as "Ascending and Descending" and "Drawing Hands".

bio|03-27|1986|Μάνουελ Νόιερ|Manuel Neuer|Manuel Neuer is a German goalkeeper. He played for Schalke and Bayern Munich and won the 2014 World Cup with Germany. He changed the role of the goalkeeper with his play outside the penalty area.

bio|03-27|2002|Μπίλι Γουάιλντερ|Billy Wilder|Billy Wilder was born in what is now Poland and emigrated to the United States. He was a director and screenwriter and directed "Some Like It Hot", "The Apartment" and "Sunset Boulevard". He won six Oscars.

bio|03-27|2006|Στάνισλαβ Λεμ|Stanislaw Lem|Stanislaw Lem was a Polish science fiction writer. He wrote the novel "Solaris", which was made into a film by Tarkovsky. His books have philosophical content and have been translated into many languages.

bio|03-28|1584|Ιβάν Δ΄|Ivan IV|Ivan IV the Terrible was the first tsar of Russia, from 1547. He expanded the state towards the Caspian and Siberia. He became notorious for his cruelty and for the "oprichnina", a period of terror.

bio|03-28|1592|Ιωάννης Αμός Κομένιος|Johann Amos Comenius|Johann Amos Comenius was a Czech educator and theologian. He is regarded as the "father of modern education". He wrote the work "The Great Didactic" and supported education for all.

bio|03-28|1868|Μαξίμ Γκόρκι|Maxim Gorky|Maxim Gorky was a Russian writer. He wrote the novel "Mother" and the play "The Lower Depths". He is regarded as the founder of socialist realism and was a friend of the Bolsheviks.

bio|03-28|1936|Μάριο Βάργκας Λιόσα|Mario Vargas Llosa|Mario Vargas Llosa was a Peruvian writer. He wrote the novels "The Time of the Hero" and "The Feast of the Goat". In 2010 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-28|1941|Βιρτζίνια Γουλφ|Virginia Woolf|Virginia Woolf took her own life in 1941 in the River Ouse in England. She was one of the most important writers of modernism and wrote "Mrs Dalloway" and "To the Lighthouse".

bio|03-28|1945|Ροντρίγκο Ντουτέρτε|Rodrigo Duterte|Rodrigo Duterte is a Filipino politician. He was mayor of Davao and from 2016 to 2022 president of the Philippines. He became known for his "war on drugs", which was linked to thousands of deaths.

bio|03-28|1969|Ντουάιτ Αϊζενχάουερ|Dwight D. Eisenhower|Dwight D. Eisenhower was an American general and supreme commander of the Allied forces in Europe in the Second World War. He was the 34th president of the United States from 1953 to 1961.

bio|03-28|1985|Μαρκ Σαγκάλ|Marc Chagall|Marc Chagall was born in Belarus and lived mainly in France. He was a painter with a dreamlike style, with images from Jewish tradition and village life, and he created the ceiling of the Paris Opera.

bio|03-28|1986|Lady Gaga|Lady Gaga|Lady Gaga, whose real name is Stefani Germanotta, is an American singer and actress. She became known with songs such as "Poker Face" and "Bad Romance", and she won an Oscar for the song "Shallow".

bio|03-29|1629|Αλέξιος|Alexis I|Alexis I Romanov was tsar of Russia from 1645 to 1676. During his reign Eastern Ukraine was annexed, and the church reform of Nikon took place. He was the father of Peter the Great.

bio|03-29|1772|Εμάνουελ Σβέντενμποργκ|Emanuel Swedenborg|Emanuel Swedenborg was a Swedish scientist, philosopher and mystic. He worked on engineering and anatomy and later wrote theological works, based on visions which he said he had.

bio|03-29|1790|Τζον Τάιλερ|John Tyler|John Tyler was the 10th president of the United States. He became president in 1841, after the death of Harrison. He supported the annexation of Texas, and during the Civil War he supported the Confederacy.

bio|03-29|1891|Ζωρζ Σερά|Georges Seurat|Georges Seurat was a French painter. He was the founder of pointillism, which uses small dots of colour. He became known for the work "A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte". He died young, at the age of 31.

bio|03-29|1899|Λαβρέντι Μπέρια|Lavrentiy Beria|Lavrentiy Beria was head of the Soviet secret police, the NKVD, under Stalin. He was responsible for many executions and imprisonments. After Stalin's death he was arrested and executed in 1953.

bio|03-29|1912|Ρόμπερτ Φάλκον Σκοτ|Robert Falcon Scott|Robert Falcon Scott was a British explorer of Antarctica. He reached the South Pole in January 1912, but the Norwegian Roald Amundsen had arrived first. He died with his team on the return journey.

bio|03-29|1968|Λούσυ Λόουλες|Lucy Lawless|Lucy Lawless is a New Zealand actress. She became known for the role of the warrior in the series "Xena: Warrior Princess". She also appeared in the series "Spartacus".

bio|03-29|2017|Αλεξέι Αλεξέγιεβιτς Αμπρικόσοφ|Alexei Abrikosov|Alexei Abrikosov was a Russian theoretical physicist. He studied superconductivity, and in 2003 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Ginzburg and Leggett.

bio|03-30|1432|Μωάμεθ Β΄ ο Πορθητής|Mehmed II the Conqueror|Mehmed II was an Ottoman sultan who captured Constantinople on 29 May 1453, bringing an end to the Byzantine Empire. He made the city the capital of the Ottoman Empire and became known as "the Conqueror".

bio|03-30|1746|Φρανθίσκο Γκόγια|Francisco Goya|Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter and engraver. He became court painter and created portraits and paintings such as "The Third of May 1808". In his last years he painted the "Black Paintings".

bio|03-30|1844|Πωλ Βερλαίν|Paul Verlaine|Paul Verlaine was a French poet of symbolism. He wrote poems with strong musicality, such as the collection "Fetes galantes", and had a turbulent relationship with Arthur Rimbaud.

bio|03-30|1853|Βίνσεντ βαν Γκογκ|Vincent van Gogh|Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter of post-Impressionism. He painted works such as "The Starry Night" and "Sunflowers" with intense colours and vivid brushstrokes. He died in 1890, at the age of 37, and his works became famous after his death.
bio|03-30|1879|Τομά Κουτύρ|Thomas Couture|Thomas Couture was a French academic painter. He became known for the large painting "The Romans of the Decadence". He had Edouard Manet as a pupil.

bio|03-30|1925|Ρούντολφ Στάινερ|Rudolf Steiner|Rudolf Steiner died in Switzerland in 1925. He was an Austrian philosopher and educator who founded anthroposophy, the Waldorf schools and biodynamic agriculture.

bio|03-30|1968|Σελίν Ντιόν|Celine Dion|Celine Dion is a Canadian singer. She became known throughout the world with the song "My Heart Will Go On" from the film "Titanic". She has sold more than 200 million records.

bio|03-30|1970|Χάινριχ Μπρύνιγκ|Heinrich Bruning|Heinrich Bruning was a German politician of the Centre Party. He was chancellor from 1930 to 1932, during the Great Depression, and he governed by presidential decrees.

bio|03-30|1986|Τζέιμς Κάγκνεϊ|James Cagney|James Cagney was an American actor. He played gangster roles and appeared in the musical "Yankee Doodle Dandy", for which he won the Oscar for Best Actor in 1943.

bio|03-31|1596|Ρενέ Ντεκάρτ|Rene Descartes|Rene Descartes was a French philosopher and mathematician. He wrote the "Discourse on the Method" and argued "I think, therefore I am". He introduced Cartesian coordinates into geometry.

bio|03-31|1685|Γιόχαν Σεμπάστιαν Μπαχ|Johann Sebastian Bach|Johann Sebastian Bach was born in Eisenach. He was a Baroque composer and organist, and he wrote the "Brandenburg Concertos", the "St Matthew Passion" and the "Mass in B minor". He is regarded as one of the greatest composers.

bio|03-31|1727|Ισαάκ Νεύτων|Isaac Newton|Isaac Newton died in London in 1727 and was buried in Westminster Abbey. He was a physicist and mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and of universal gravitation, and developed calculus.

bio|03-31|1732|Γιόζεφ Χάυντν|Joseph Haydn|Joseph Haydn was an Austrian composer of the Classical period. He wrote more than 100 symphonies and many string quartets, and is regarded as the "father of the symphony". He was a friend of Mozart and the teacher of Beethoven.

bio|03-31|1855|Σαρλότ Μπροντέ|Charlotte Bronte|Charlotte Bronte was an English writer. She wrote the novel "Jane Eyre" under the pseudonym Currer Bell. She was the sister of Emily and Anne Bronte and died in 1855.

bio|03-31|1890|Ουίλιαμ Λώρενς Μπραγκ|William Lawrence Bragg|William Lawrence Bragg was born in Australia and was a British physicist. Together with his father he developed X-ray crystallography, and in 1915, at the age of 25, he became the youngest person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
bio|03-31|1914|Οκτάβιο Πας|Octavio Paz|Octavio Paz was a Mexican poet, essayist and diplomat. He wrote the essay "The Labyrinth of Solitude". In 1990 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-31|1948|Αλ Γκορ|Al Gore|Al Gore is an American Democratic politician. He was vice president of the United States under Bill Clinton and lost to George W. Bush in 2000. He worked on environmental issues and in 2007 was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|03-31|1995|Selena|Selena|Selena Quintanilla was an American singer of Mexican origin, known as the "Queen of Tejano music". She was murdered in 1995, at the age of 23, by the president of her fan club.

bio|03-31|2016|Ίμρε Κέρτες|Imre Kertesz|Imre Kertesz was a Hungarian writer. He survived Auschwitz and Buchenwald and wrote the novel "Fatelessness" about that experience. In 2002 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-01|1809|Νικολάι Γκόγκολ|Nikolai Gogol|Nikolai Gogol was a Russian writer of Ukrainian origin. He wrote "Dead Souls", "The Government Inspector" and the short story "The Overcoat". He had a significant influence on Russian literature.

bio|04-01|1815|Όττο φον Μπίσμαρκ|Otto von Bismarck|Otto von Bismarck was a Prussian politician. As chancellor of Prussia he led the unification of Germany in 1871 and became the first chancellor of the German Empire. He was known as the "Iron Chancellor".

bio|04-01|1908|Αβραάμ Μάσλοου|Abraham Maslow|Abraham Maslow was an American psychologist. He is known for the "hierarchy of needs", often presented as a pyramid, and he was a leading representative of humanistic psychology.

bio|04-01|1920|Τοσίρο Μιφούνε|Toshiro Mifune|Toshiro Mifune was a Japanese actor. He appeared in many films by Akira Kurosawa, such as "Rashomon", "Seven Samurai" and "Throne of Blood". He was the best-known Japanese actor in the West.

bio|04-01|1929|Μίλαν Κούντερα|Milan Kundera|Milan Kundera was a Czech writer who lived in France. He wrote the novels "The Joke" and "The Unbearable Lightness of Being". His works examine totalitarianism and personal freedom.

bio|04-01|1968|Λεβ Λαντάου|Lev Landau|Lev Landau was a Soviet theoretical physicist. He studied superfluidity and the physics of condensed matter, and in 1962 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1968, after injuries in a car accident.

bio|04-01|1984|Μάρβιν Γκέι|Marvin Gaye|Marvin Gaye was an American soul singer and a Motown artist. He wrote "What's Going On" and "Let's Get It On". He was shot and killed by his father in 1984, one day before his 45th birthday.

bio|04-01|2017|Γεβγκένι Γεφτουσένκο|Yevgeny Yevtushenko|Yevgeny Yevtushenko was a Russian poet. He became known in the 1960s with the poem "Babi Yar" about the massacre of Jews in Kiev. He was a voice of the thaw in the Soviet Union.
bio|04-01|2025|Βαλ Κίλμερ|Val Kilmer|Val Kilmer was an American actor. He became known for the films "Top Gun", "The Doors", "Tombstone" and "Batman Forever", in which he played Batman.

bio|04-02|1725|Τζάκομο Καζανόβα|Giacomo Casanova|Giacomo Casanova was an Italian writer and adventurer from Venice. He lived through many journeys and romantic adventures, which he described in his memoirs "The Story of My Life".

bio|04-02|1805|Χανς Κρίστιαν Άντερσεν|Hans Christian Andersen|Hans Christian Andersen was a Danish writer. He wrote fairy tales such as "The Little Mermaid", "The Ugly Duckling" and "The Emperor's New Clothes", which became famous all over the world. He died in 1875.

bio|04-02|1840|Εμίλ Ζολά|Emile Zola|Emile Zola was a French writer and the leading representative of naturalism. He wrote the series of novels "Les Rougon-Macquart", including "Germinal" and "Nana". With the article "J'accuse" he defended Dreyfus.

bio|04-02|1872|Σάμιουελ Μορς|Samuel Morse|Samuel Morse was an American painter and inventor. He developed the electric telegraph and, together with Alfred Vail, the Morse code. In 1844 the first telegraph message was sent from Washington to Baltimore.
bio|04-02|1914|Άλεκ Γκίνες|Alec Guinness|Alec Guinness was an English actor. He won the Oscar for Best Actor for "The Bridge on the River Kwai" and played Obi-Wan Kenobi in "Star Wars".

bio|04-02|1914|Πάουλ Γιόχαν Λούντβιχ φον Χάιζε|Paul von Heyse|Paul von Heyse was a German writer. He wrote novellas, poems and plays, and in 1910 he became the first German to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1914.
bio|04-02|1939|Μάρβιν Γκέι|Marvin Gaye|Marvin Gaye was born in Washington and became one of the most important singers of Motown. His 1971 album "What's Going On" became a landmark of soul music.

bio|04-02|1974|Ζωρζ Πομπιντού|Georges Pompidou|Georges Pompidou was a French politician and president of France from 1969 until his death. He was prime minister under de Gaulle. The Pompidou Centre in Paris is named after him.

bio|04-02|1995|Χάνες Αλφβέν|Hannes Alfven|Hannes Alfven was a Swedish physicist. He developed magnetohydrodynamics, and in 1970 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his study of electromagnetic phenomena in plasmas.

bio|04-03|1682|Μπαρτολομέ Εστέμπαν Μουρίγιο|Bartolome Esteban Murillo|Bartolome Esteban Murillo was a Spanish Baroque painter from Seville. He painted religious subjects, with many paintings of the Virgin Mary, and scenes of everyday life of street children.

bio|04-03|1849|Γιούλιους Σλοβάτσκι|Juliusz Slowacki|Juliusz Slowacki was a Polish poet and playwright of the Romantic movement. He lived in exile in Paris. He wrote the plays "Kordian" and "Beniowski".

bio|04-03|1897|Γιοχάνες Μπραμς|Johannes Brahms|Johannes Brahms was a German composer of the Romantic period. He wrote four symphonies, the "German Requiem" and concertos for piano and violin, and he is known for the "Hungarian Dances".

bio|04-03|1922|Ντόρις Ντέι|Doris Day|Doris Day was an American actress and singer. She appeared in musicals and comedies, such as "The Man Who Knew Too Much", where she sang "Que Sera, Sera". Later she devoted herself to animal protection.

bio|04-03|1924|Μάρλον Μπράντο|Marlon Brando|Marlon Brando was an American actor. He won Oscars for "On the Waterfront" and "The Godfather", and he appeared in "A Streetcar Named Desire" and "Apocalypse Now". He influenced the style of acting.

bio|04-03|1930|Χέλμουτ Κολ|Helmut Kohl|Helmut Kohl was a German politician of the Christian Democratic Union. He was chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998 and led the reunification of the country in 1990. He was a strong supporter of European unification.

bio|04-03|1958|Άλεκ Μπάλντουιν|Alec Baldwin|Alec Baldwin is an American actor. He became known for the series "30 Rock" and for films such as "The Hunt for Red October". He is the eldest of the Baldwin brothers.

bio|04-03|1961|Έντι Μέρφι|Eddie Murphy|Eddie Murphy is an American actor and comedian. He became known on "Saturday Night Live" and in films such as "Beverly Hills Cop" and "The Nutty Professor". He gave the voice of the Donkey in "Shrek".

bio|04-03|1991|Γκράχαμ Γκρην|Graham Greene|Graham Greene was an English writer. He wrote the novels "Brighton Rock", "The Third Man" and "Our Man in Havana". His works often have religious or political content.

bio|04-04|188|Καρακάλλας|Caracalla|Caracalla was a Roman emperor from 211 to 217. In 212, with the Constitutio Antoniniana, he gave Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the empire. He built the Baths of Caracalla in Rome.

bio|04-04|1841|Ουίλιαμ Χένρι Χάρισον|William Henry Harrison|William Henry Harrison, the 9th president of the United States, died only a month after his inauguration, on 4 April 1841. His presidency is the shortest in the history of the United States.
bio|04-04|1928|Μάγια Άντζελου|Maya Angelou|Maya Angelou was an American poet and writer. She wrote the autobiography "I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings" and was an activist for civil rights.

bio|04-04|1929|Καρλ Μπεντς|Karl Benz|Karl Benz was a German engineer and inventor. In 1885-1886 he built the first car with a petrol engine, the "Benz Patent-Motorwagen". He founded the company Benz & Cie, which became part of Mercedes-Benz.

bio|04-04|1932|Αντρέι Ταρκόφσκι|Andrei Tarkovsky|Andrei Tarkovsky was a Russian film director. He directed "Andrei Rublev", "Solaris", "Stalker" and "The Sacrifice". He is regarded as one of the greatest directors, with a poetic and philosophical style.

bio|04-04|1965|Ρόμπερτ Ντάουνι Τζούνιορ|Robert Downey Jr.|Robert Downey Jr. is an American actor. He became known for the role of Tony Stark in "Iron Man" and in the Avengers films, and he won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for "Oppenheimer".

bio|04-04|1968|Μάρτιν Λούθερ Κινγκ|Martin Luther King Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated on 4 April 1968 in Memphis, Tennessee. He was the best-known leader of the civil rights movement and had received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.

bio|04-04|1979|Χιθ Λέτζερ|Heath Ledger|Heath Ledger was an Australian actor. He became known for the films "A Knight's Tale" and "Brokeback Mountain", and he played the Joker in "The Dark Knight". He died in 2008 at the age of 28.

bio|04-04|2013|Ρότζερ Ίμπερτ|Roger Ebert|Roger Ebert was an American film critic and screenwriter. For decades he wrote for the Chicago Sun-Times and presented a television programme of film criticism. In 1975 he won the Pulitzer Prize for Criticism.

bio|04-05|1588|Τόμας Χομπς|Thomas Hobbes|Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher. In his work "Leviathan" he argued that people must hand over power to a strong sovereign to avoid a war of all against all.

bio|04-05|1900|Σπένσερ Τρέισι|Spencer Tracy|Spencer Tracy was an American actor. He won two consecutive Oscars for Best Actor, for the films "Captains Courageous" and "Boys Town". He appeared in many films with Katharine Hepburn.

bio|04-05|1908|Μπέτι Ντέιβις|Bette Davis|Bette Davis was an American actress. She won two Oscars for Best Actress and was one of the biggest stars of Hollywood, with films such as "All About Eve" and "What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?".

bio|04-05|1916|Γκρέγκορι Πεκ|Gregory Peck|Gregory Peck was an American actor. He won the Oscar for Best Actor for "To Kill a Mockingbird", in which he played the lawyer Atticus Finch. He also appeared in "Roman Holiday".

bio|04-05|1947|Γκλόρια Αρόγιο|Gloria Macapagal Arroyo|Gloria Macapagal Arroyo is a Filipino politician. She was president of the Philippines from 2001 to 2010 and later a member of the House of Representatives. She faced charges of corruption.

bio|04-05|1964|Ντάγκλας Μακάρθουρ|Douglas MacArthur|Douglas MacArthur died in 1964. He was an American general who led the forces in the Pacific in the Second World War and headed the occupation of Japan.

bio|04-05|1975|Τσιανγκ Κάι Σεκ|Chiang Kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek was a Chinese soldier and politician. He led the Kuomintang and, after its defeat in the civil war by the communists in 1949, moved the government to Taiwan, where he was president until his death.

bio|04-05|1994|Κερτ Κομπέιν|Kurt Cobain|Kurt Cobain took his own life around 5 April 1994 in Seattle, and his body was found on 8 April. He was the singer of Nirvana, who became famous with "Smells Like Teen Spirit".

bio|04-05|2005|Σολ Μπέλοου|Saul Bellow|Saul Bellow was a Canadian-American writer. He wrote the novels "The Adventures of Augie March" and "Humboldt's Gift". In 1976 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-06|1483|Ραφαήλ|Raphael|Raphael was born in Urbino and became a painter and architect of the Italian Renaissance. He painted "The School of Athens" in the Vatican and many Madonnas. He died young, at the age of 37.

bio|04-06|1520|Ραφαήλ|Raphael|Raphael died in Rome in 1520, at only 37 years old, according to tradition on the same date on which he had been born. He was one of the greatest painters of the Renaissance, with works such as "The School of Athens".

bio|04-06|1528|Άλμπρεχτ Ντύρερ|Albrecht Durer|Albrecht Durer was a German painter, engraver and art theorist from Nuremberg. He became famous for his woodcuts and copperplate engravings, such as "Knight, Death and the Devil".

bio|04-06|1820|Ναντάρ|Nadar|Nadar, whose real name was Gaspard-Felix Tournachon, was a French photographer, journalist and caricaturist. He photographed many personalities of Paris and took the first aerial photographs.

bio|04-06|1826|Γκυστάβ Μορώ|Gustave Moreau|Gustave Moreau was a French painter of symbolism. He painted mythological and biblical subjects in rich colours. He taught Matisse and Rouault at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

bio|04-06|1904|Κουρτ Γκέοργκ Κίζινγκερ|Kurt Georg Kiesinger|Kurt Georg Kiesinger was a German politician of the Christian Democratic Union. He was chancellor of West Germany from 1966 to 1969. He had been a member of the Nazi Party.
bio|04-06|1963|Ραφαέλ Κορρέα|Rafael Correa|Rafael Correa is an economist and politician from Ecuador. He was president of Ecuador from 2007 to 2017 and followed a left-wing economic policy.

bio|04-06|1971|Ιγκόρ Στραβίνσκι|Igor Stravinsky|Igor Stravinsky was a Russian composer who lived in France and the United States. He wrote the ballets "The Firebird", "Petrushka" and "The Rite of Spring", which changed the music of the twentieth century.

bio|04-06|1992|Ισαάκ Ασίμωφ|Isaac Asimov|Isaac Asimov died in 1992 in New York. He was a Russian-American science fiction writer and biochemist, with more than 400 book titles, including the "Foundation" series.

bio|04-07|1498|Κάρολος Η΄|Charles VIII|Charles VIII was king of France from 1483 to 1498. In 1494 he invaded Italy and began the Italian Wars. He died suddenly in 1498, after hitting his head on a door.

bio|04-07|1770|Ουίλιαμ Γουόρντσγουορθ|William Wordsworth|William Wordsworth was an English poet of the Romantic movement. He wrote the "Lyrical Ballads" with Coleridge, and the poem "Daffodils". He was Poet Laureate from 1843.

bio|04-07|1789|Αμπντούλ Χαμίτ Α΄|Abdul Hamid I|Abdul Hamid I was an Ottoman sultan from 1774 to 1789. During his reign the Ottoman Empire was defeated by Russia and Crimea was lost. After his death he was succeeded by Selim III.
bio|04-07|1889|Γκαμπριέλα Μιστράλ|Gabriela Mistral|Gabriela Mistral was a Chilean poet and teacher. In 1945 she became the first Latin American to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-07|1944|Γκέρχαρντ Σρέντερ|Gerhard Schroder|Gerhard Schroder is a German politician of the Social Democratic Party. He was chancellor of Germany from 1998 to 2005 and promoted the "Agenda 2010" reforms.

bio|04-07|1947|Χένρυ Φορντ|Henry Ford|Henry Ford was an American businessman and founder of the Ford Motor Company. He created the Model T and introduced the assembly line, which made the car affordable for the general public.

bio|04-07|1954|Τζάκι Τσαν|Jackie Chan|Jackie Chan was born in Hong Kong and is an actor and martial arts expert. He is known for action films with comic elements, such as "Rush Hour", in which he performs the stunts himself.
bio|04-07|1964|Ράσελ Κρόου|Russell Crowe|Russell Crowe is a New Zealand actor. He won the Oscar for Best Actor for "Gladiator" in 2000 and appeared in "A Beautiful Mind" and "Les Miserables".

bio|04-08|217|Καρακάλλας|Caracalla|Caracalla was murdered in 217 during a campaign against the Parthians, by one of his soldiers, in a plot planned by Macrinus, who succeeded him. He had become famous for the Edict of 212, which gave Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the empire.

bio|04-08|1605|Φίλιππος Δ΄|Philip IV|Philip IV was king of Spain from 1621 to 1665. He became known as the patron of the painter Velazquez. During his reign Spain lost power, and Portugal became independent in 1640.

bio|04-08|1859|Έντμουντ Χούσερλ|Edmund Husserl|Edmund Husserl was a German philosopher and the founder of phenomenology. He was a professor at Freiburg and wrote "Logical Investigations" and "Ideas". He influenced Heidegger and Sartre.

bio|04-08|1892|Μαίρη Πίκφορντ|Mary Pickford|Mary Pickford was a Canadian actress and producer of silent films and one of the biggest stars of her era. She founded United Artists together with Charlie Chaplin, Douglas Fairbanks and D. W. Griffith.

bio|04-08|1938|Κόφι Ανάν|Kofi Annan|Kofi Annan was a Ghanaian diplomat. He served as Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1997 to 2006. In 2001 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize jointly with the UN. He died in 2018.

bio|04-08|1973|Πάμπλο Πικάσο|Pablo Picasso|Pablo Picasso died in France in 1973. He was a Spanish painter and sculptor and one of the founders of Cubism. He painted "Guernica" and "Les Demoiselles d'Avignon".

bio|04-08|1984|Πιοτρ Καπίτσα|Pyotr Kapitsa|Pyotr Kapitsa was a Russian physicist. He studied low-temperature physics and the superfluidity of liquid helium. In 1978 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
